title: Seat a thermostat square in a vertical engine housing, valve up, let go, then push the water inlet over two studs
instruction: Replace the engine's thermostat: seat the new thermostat in the housing with its spring end toward the engine and its jiggle valve at the top, and let go of it, then push the water inlet home over both studs until it sits flush on the housing, and leave it on the studs over the thermostat.
context: Automotive service technicians and mechanics, 676,570 employed in the US in May 2023 (BLS OEWS 49-3023), have as a Core task on O*NET 49-3023.00: 'Repair and service air conditioning, heating, engine cooling, and electrical systems.' A thermostat replacement is one of the routine jobs in that duty. The technician sets the new thermostat, seal fitted, square into the housing's recess with its jiggle valve at the top, then pushes the water inlet over the studs before running the nuts down. A cocked thermostat pinches its seal and leaks coolant; one put in backwards leaves the engine to overheat; a jiggle valve left low traps air behind the thermostat when the system is refilled. It is hard because the 60 mm seal must enter a recess on a vertical face with 0.5 mm of radial clearance, clocked to within 10 degrees, and stay there by itself while the other hand brings the 320 g inlet, whose 10 mm holes must find two 8 mm studs before its face closes flush over the thermostat.
setup: Two YAM arms at the near edge of a table; positions are (x forward from the arm bases, y left) in cm, heights above the table. A cut-away engine front section stands on the table, its thermostat housing face vertical at x 42, facing the arms. The housing has a round recess 61.0 mm across and 6 mm deep, with a 1.5 mm lead-in chamfer and the coolant passage behind it, its axis at y 0 and 15 cm above the table, and two M8 studs 92 mm apart (y -4.6 and 4.6) standing 30 mm proud, with chamfered ends. A rubber shop mat lies in front of it. On the mat, as a mechanic lays out the parts: the new thermostat (Stant 46128, 2017 Camry 3.5 L 2GR-FE: 60.0 mm seal, 56.0 mm flange, 110 g) stands on its spring end at (30, -12), bridge up, its jiggle valve pointing to the side; the cast aluminium water inlet (Dorman 902-5932 class, 320 g: a two-ear flange with 10 mm stud holes, a domed cap and a bent hose neck) lies at (38, 12) with its face toward the engine, resting on the lower edge of its flange and the end of its hose neck. The start pose is the same every run.
scoring: Read each step (20 Hz) from both parts' poses and both whole grippers. 0.3: thermostat seated (the seal's mid-plane 3 +/- 1 mm behind the housing face (its back on the 6 mm seat), centred within 1.5 mm, axis within 3 degrees, spring end in) for 1 s, no gripper part within 10 mm of it, inlet over 10 mm from the housing face. 0.6: as 0.3 with the jiggle valve within 10 degrees of top, still so at the end. 1.0: then the inlet pushed flush (holes on both studs, face within 1 mm of the housing all round) for 1 s and left on both studs (holes within 3 mm of the studs' axes, face within 20 mm of the housing) over the seated thermostat, valve up, both grippers over 10 mm away for 1 s. Inlet counts neck down or up. Void (0): seated, then cocked or out at the end. Real check: during the 1 s let-go before the inlet comes, the top camera shows the bridge's legs equally proud within 2.5 mm, and the bridge top, read with a straightedge across it and a caliper depth rod to the housing face, is within 1 mm of the height measured once the same way on the hand-seated real thermostat (cocked reads outside it); side camera at bore height reads the flush gap at top and bottom, top camera over the housing at both ears; front camera and valve marks scribed at +/-10 degrees; seal depth at the flange face, four-point depth gauge, after lifting the inlet off.
reset_notes: Lift the water inlet off the studs and lay it back on the mat, face toward the engine, on its flange edge and hose end; pull the thermostat out of its recess (the seal sits in the 61.0 mm recess with 0.5 mm clearance; in a real engine section it is a light push fit) and stand it on its spring end on the mat. Nothing is consumed; fit a new seal if it has been pinched.
fidelity: Rigid bodies on GPU. The engine section is fixed; the thermostat (110 g) and inlet (320 g) are free, colliding bodies. The recess, chamfer, studs and tips are collision meshes: the thermostat stays in by contact and friction only, the inlet rides the studs on its holes, no joints or snaps. The seal is rigid with 0.5 mm radial clearance kept on purpose (real: a light squeeze fit, seat diameter unpublished); crossbar 12 x 1 mm sheet. No nuts: released, the inlet tips on the studs.
